text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--A majority of Danes consider that Greenland and the Faroe Islands' adhesion to the Danish commonwealth under the rule of Denmark is advantageous for all three parties despite tension in recent years between the North Atlantic provinces and Copenhagen, according to a new survey.
--1997 looks like being a record year for criminal money laundering, with 145 cases of dubious financial transactions reported so far this year by Danish banks.

--The U.S. dollar has hit a record peak for the 1990s of 7.02 crowns making Danish export industries more competitive with American firms in overseas markets, the Confederation of Danish Industries said.
--The Labour Movement's Business Council warns against the dangers for the economy of uncontrolled wage rises in Denmark.

--Danes are lodging complaints against insurance companies to the Danish Insurance Appeal Tribunal as never before, but most of the dissatisfaction is with smaller firms, not the three leading insurers.
--Demand for Danish mortgage credit bonds is expected to be sizeable in the next few years, pointing to a possible major narrowing of yields between state and mortgage bonds, according to CSFB.
--Denmark's building and construction sector is headed for a major boom, according to a forecast by Germany's Ifo Institute of Economy in Munich.
